invariants.rationale: The method immediately dereferences tile (calling getProperties()), so tile is expected to be non-null.
tileElement is dereferenced to call getAttribute and getChildByName, so it must be non-null for correct execution.
The method stores the result of tile.getProperties() and subsequently uses it, implying it should not be null.
If the 'terrain' attribute is present and not null, it may be an empty string, otherwise it is null.
If a child named "properties" exists, it may be used; otherwise it is null, and both cases are anticipated by later code.
